label: HJR 4
t: Only Legislature may legalize marijuana and drugs
what: Amends the constitution so that only the Idaho Legislature has the power to legalize marijuana, narcotics or other psychoactive substances. This would remove citizens' ability to legalize them through ballot initiatives.
y: Only the Legislature could legalize marijuana, narcotics or other psychoactive substances.
n: Citizens keep the option of legalizing such substances by initiative; the Legislature keeps its existing power.
fiscal: Not more than $200,000 (cost of placing the measure on the ballot).

label: HJR 6
t: English as official state language in constitution
what: Adds to the constitution that English is Idaho's official language and that, except where federal law requires otherwise, English shall be used in all public proceedings, documents, public instruction and other public acts. English is already the official language by a 2007 statute.
y: English becomes the official language in the constitution, with English required in public proceedings and instruction except where federal law requires otherwise.
n: English stays official only by statute, which the Legislature can change.
fiscal: Up to $300,000 for voter pamphlet publication (per the legislative fiscal note).
con: Rep. John Gannon (concern over foreign-language and ESL instruction)

label: Advisory Question
what: Asks voters to pick one of six firearms as Idaho's official state gun: Winchester Model 1894, Winchester Model 1873, Colt Single Action Army 'Peacemaker', M1 Garand, Colt M1911, or Remington Model 700. The result is advisory; a designation would require a separate law.
y: Voters register a preference among the six firearms.
n: Not a yes/no question; no law changes either way.
fiscal: No specific fiscal note; ballot costs covered by the Secretary of State's existing appropriation.

label: Proposition 1
what: Creates a statutory right to reproductive freedom and privacy, including abortion up to fetal viability and afterward in medical emergencies, and rights to contraception, fertility treatment, and prenatal and postpartum care. It bars enforcement of current abortion laws that conflict, limits restrictions to those meeting a compelling state interest in health, and shields patients and providers from penalties. Takes effect January 1, 2027.
y: Abortion becomes legal until fetal viability (later in medical emergencies), and related reproductive-care rights are written into state law.
n: Current law stays: abortion is banned except to prevent the pregnant woman's death or, in the first trimester, for reported rape or incest.
fiscal: Idaho Division of Financial Management: about $3,100–$7,800 a year in state Medicaid costs.
pro: Idahoans United for Women and Families, Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates
con: Idaho Family Policy Center, Idaho Chooses Life, Right to Life Idaho, Too Extreme for Idaho, Roman Catholic Diocese of Boise
